name: nuckelavee

attributes.attribute: a monster of Scottish folk tale
a single eye on a horse-shaped head
flippers in place of legs and red flesh
lived in the sea and sprang out to kill
a relative of the Water Horse and the Nygel of Shetland

sources: Douglas, George. Scottish Fairy and Folk Tales. West Yorkshire: Ep Publishing, 1977, 160 ff.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The nuckelavee is a figure of Scottish lore. On Orkney, the isles above Scotland, folk told of being set upon by a monster. It has a horse's body and a single fixed eye above a head the shape of a horse. Its limbs are flukes, not legs, and the flesh is red. It dwelled in the sea and would spring out to slay a person or a cow. The only shield was the race across a stream, which the living thing could not bear. Some call it a kin of the Water Horse or of the Nygel of Shetland.

okr.objective: Present the nuckelavee as a sea monster of the Or well.
key_results: The nuckelavee had a horse body and a one-eyed human-looking head in Orking tale.
It lived in the sea and leapt out onto the shore to kill humans or a cow.
A quick stride across fresh water would rob the sea-being of its power.
The monster is tied to the Water Horse and the Nygel of Shetland.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
